junction.name: Montana Avenue Northeast & 17th Street Northeast, Washington DC

claims.text: Montana Avenue Northeast & 17th Street Northeast had 51 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 pedestrians injured, 1 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.5 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.
The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: not shown (at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero).
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 2.8 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $950,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $524,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is responsible for Montana Avenue Northeast, West Virginia Avenue Northeast, unnamed (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for New York Avenue Northeast (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
A request letter to the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) and the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
